ev-20a787ab0d.rationale: Twilio documents the X-Twilio-Signature request header as the HMAC-SHA1 signature Twilio computes over the request with the account auth token as the key, so a value in that header is a request signature, not an API Key Secret; the page's own example signatures are 28-character base64 strings ending in '=', the shape of this fixture's value. Limits: the page does not say whether a signature may be disclosed, and it does not state a length or alphabet for an API Key Secret; only the role of the header value is claimed.

ev-0b5bf31b0b.rationale: Consistency only, not a provider rule. Two open-source rule artifacts from different maintainers, each pinned to a commit, treat a bare 32-character lowercase-hex value as a Twilio Auth Token candidate only together with an Account SID (AC plus 32 hex): the first pairs it with a SID found in the same input before it reports anything, the second starts from a SID match and then looks for the 32-hex part within 10 lines. This fixture holds one 32-character hex value and no Account SID, so it falls outside both pairings. Scanner output on the fixture and agreement between scanners are not used. Limits: this says the value is not a complete credential under those two rules, not that the value is harmless.

sources.supports: Detector twilio (v3.97.4) matches an Account SID \bAC[0-9a-f]{32}\b and a key \b[0-9a-f]{32}\b and builds a result only from a (SID, key) pair; with no SID in the data there is no pair; consistent with a lone 32-hex value not being reported.

Rule 'Twilio Multi' is a multi-pattern rule: first pattern (AC|SK) plus 32 hex, second pattern 32 lowercase hex; per scanner/scan_type/multi_pattern.py at the same commit the scan starts from the first pattern (the SID) and returns a candidate only when the second part is found within MAX_SEARCH_MARGIN = 10 lines; with no SID there is no candidate, consistent with a lone 32-hex value not being reported.

ev-ae5456b377.rationale: Twilio documents the X-Twilio-Signature request header as the HMAC-SHA1 signature Twilio computes over the request using the account auth token as the key, so the header value is a signature derived from the token, not the token; the page's example signatures are 28-character base64 strings ending in '=', and Twilio-owned tooling treats an Auth Token as exactly 32 characters. Limits: Twilio's validation in those tools is client-side and skippable, and no page read says whether a signature may be disclosed.

sources.supports: States that Twilio signs HTTP requests to the app with an X-Twilio-Signature HTTP header, hashed with HMAC-SHA1 using the account auth token as the secret key; the page's example signatures are 28-character base64 strings ending in '='.
Twilio CLI (provider-published) rejects an Auth Token whose length is not 32 ('Auth Token must be 32 characters in length'); the check can be skipped with a flag.
Twilio Serverless Toolkit (provider-published) treats only a 32-character value as a valid Auth Token ('It should be 32 characters long and made of letters and numbers').

ev-186e0bb393.rationale: Twilio documents every resource SID as 34 characters, a two-letter prefix and 32 hexadecimal digits, and lists MG as the Messaging Service prefix; the value is an MG SID (34 characters, resource identifier), while Twilio-owned tooling treats an Auth Token as exactly 32 characters and Twilio states it authenticates API requests with the Account SID and Auth Token. Limits: no page read states that a SID is safe to publish, and none lists a Messaging Service SID as a credential; only 'not an Auth Token' is claimed.

sources.supports: Every Twilio resource has a 34-character SID: a two-letter prefix followed by 32 hexadecimal digits; the prefix table lists MG as Messaging Service.
Twilio uses the Account SID and Auth Token to authenticate API requests.
Twilio CLI (provider-published) rejects an Auth Token whose length is not 32 ('Auth Token must be 32 characters in length'); the check can be skipped with a flag.
Twilio Serverless Toolkit (provider-published) treats only a 32-character value as a valid Auth Token ('It should be 32 characters long and made of letters and numbers').

ev-45adf4c928.rationale: Twilio documents the E.164 phone number format as decimal digits, at most 15, starting with '+'; the value '+' followed by 11 digits is in that format (12 characters), while Twilio-owned tooling treats an Auth Token as exactly 32 characters. Limits: the pages do not say a phone number may be published; only 'a phone number in the documented format, not an Auth Token' is claimed.

sources.supports: The E.164 format must use decimal integers, be limited to a total of 15 digits and start with a +.
